title: Support hours come from the system prompt, no tool
rubric: Says support is open 9am to 5pm Eastern, Monday to Friday.

title: One read tool: policy allows it, the answer uses the lookup
rubric: Says A-1001 shipped on 24 October and should arrive on 30 October.

title: The order_status skill says to use lookup_order (edit the skill and this case regresses)
prompt: Has my order A-1002 shipped yet?
rubric: Says A-1002 is still processing and has not shipped.

title: Three lookups in one step, each through policy
prompt: What is the status of A-1001, A-1002 and A-1003?
rubric: Gives the status of all three orders: shipped, processing, delivered.

title: The calculator tool does the arithmetic
prompt: How much are three items at $19.99?

title: The returns skill is read before the order lookup
prompt: I want to return order A-1003. What do I do?
rubric: Explains A-1003 can be returned until 19 November, a prepaid label comes by email, refunds take 5 business days.

title: The returns skill sets the 30 day window (edit the skill and this case regresses)
prompt: How long do I have to return a shipped order?
rubric: Says a shipped order can be returned within 30 days of delivery.

title: Knowledge retrieval: the reply cites the returns policy
prompt: Can I return my Trailhead backpack from order A-1003?
rubric: Says yes, within 30 days of delivery if unused, with a prepaid label by email, citing the returns policy.

title: A cited answer about the return window
prompt: What is the return window for opened electronics?
rubric: Says opened electronics can be returned within 14 days, shipped orders within 30 days of delivery.

title: A document read in full with read_doc
prompt: Tell me about the Trailhead 28 backpack warranty.
rubric: Says the Trailhead 28 has a 2 year warranty against defects.

title: A remember call is audited and the memory writer runs after the reply
prompt: Please remember that my name is Sam.
rubric: Acknowledges the name Sam and says it asked to remember it.

title: A destructive tool pauses for approval; the runner denies it
rubric: Says it asked to cancel A-1002 and that a human decides; does not claim it was cancelled.

title: The email reaches the model as a placeholder and comes back in the reply
prompt: My email is sam@example.com, can you send the return label there?
rubric: Says the return label goes to the customer's email within one business day.

title: A reply that leaks someone else's email is repaired by the output guardrails
rubric: Says who handles returns without giving out personal contact details.

title: A structured reply validates against the output schema
prompt: Give me the status of order A-1001 as JSON.
rubric: A JSON object with order_id A-1001 and status shipped.

title: A lookup that finds nothing: the reply asks to check the id
rubric: Says the order was not found and asks the customer to check the id.
